statement: Nine points are equally spaced around a circle and numbered $1$ through $9$ in order. Starting at point $1$, Zoe draws a segment to point $5$, then to point $9$, then to point $4$, and so on, each time moving $4$ points forward around the circle, until she returns to point $1$. The segments form a nine-pointed star. What is the degree measure of the angle at each tip of the star?

choices.misconception: I found the $40^\circ$ arc cut off between the two segments at a tip and used it as the angle, without halving it.
I thought connecting every fourth point works like connecting every third point, which draws equilateral triangles with $60^\circ$ corners.
I subtracted one $40^\circ$ step from the $140^\circ$ interior angle of a regular nine-sided polygon.
I used the interior angle of a regular nine-sided polygon, $\frac{7 \cdot 180^\circ}{9}$, as the angle at each tip.

hints: The angle at a tip has its vertex on the circle, so it is an inscribed angle. Which arc does it cut off?
At point $1$ the two segments go to point $5$ and to point $6$ (Zoe reaches point $1$ from point $6$). The tip angle cuts off the arc from $5$ to $6$ that does not contain point $1$.
That arc is one ninth of the circle, $40^\circ$, and an inscribed angle is half of the arc it cuts off.

solutions.reliable: Zoe visits $1, 5, 9, 4, 8, 3, 7, 2, 6$ and then returns to $1$, so every point is a tip, and by symmetry all tips have the same angle. At point $1$ the two segments go to points $5$ and $6$. The angle at point $1$ is an inscribed angle cutting off the arc from $5$ to $6$ that does not contain point $1$. That arc is one step, $\frac{360^\circ}{9} = 40^\circ$, so the tip angle is $\frac{40^\circ}{2} = 20^\circ$.
solutions.elegant: Walk around the star. At each tip with angle $t$ you turn by $180^\circ - t$. Moving $4$ points forward each time, you travel around the circle $4$ times in all ($9$ steps of $4$ is $36$ points, which is $4$ laps), so your total turning is $4 \cdot 360^\circ = 1440^\circ$. Then $9(180^\circ - t) = 1440^\circ$, so $180^\circ - t = 160^\circ$ and $t = 20^\circ$.

author: Devansh Sanghavi
